intro: You are at Çavuştepe, an ancient city in Van province from the 8th century BC. This was an Urartian fortress, with a royal palace and a temple, and an irrigation canal that is still in use.
history: Çavuştepe was built by King Sarduri II. And look below the site: the Şamran canal has watered the fields here for 2,700 years.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Upper fortress and the Temple of Haldi, then the Palace kitchen, and finally the Şamran canal.
facts: Did you know? This was the fortress of the Urartian king Sarduri II, and the site of one of the oldest known lavatories in Anatolia. Look closely at the temple of Haldi: its polished basalt blocks fit without mortar, smooth as glass, and they are dressed so finely that a knife will not pass between them.
outro: This brings our journey through Çavuştepe to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for listening, and enjoy your visit.
